subjects.title: Product Hero, Clear & Isolated
subjects.text: Make [product] the unmistakable hero: fully visible, correctly proportioned, and isolated against a clean, simple setting with generous breathing room. Preserve its exact silhouette, color, finish, branding, and construction. Use only restrained supporting elements; the image must let a customer understand what the product is within the first second.

subjects.title: Product in Natural Use
subjects.text: Show [product] being used in one believable, relevant moment by [subject]. Make the action clear enough to explain purpose, scale, and handling while keeping important product features visible. The interaction should feel naturally observed, with realistic grip, posture, contact, and environment—not a posed demonstration.

subjects.title: Tactile Detail Subject
subjects.text: Treat [specific product detail] as the subject: show the material, weave, grain, stitching, closure, finish, or interface at a scale that makes quality inspectable. Include just enough surrounding context to identify the product. Use light that reveals real surface behavior and avoid decorative blur that hides the evidence.

subjects.title: Scale & Proportion Proof
subjects.text: Show [product] beside or in the hands of a familiar human or contextual reference so its true size, capacity, fit, and proportions are immediately understandable. Keep the scale reference natural and secondary. Preserve perspective and product dimensions accurately; do not use an angle that exaggerates or obscures size.

subjects.title: Variant Lineup
subjects.text: Present [product family] as a clear, coordinated lineup of [variants/colors/sizes]. Give each item equal visual importance, consistent orientation, and readable spacing while preserving the differences customers need to compare. Keep the background and light neutral so the product variations—not styling noise—carry the image.

subjects.title: Unboxing Moment
subjects.text: Center a genuine unboxing moment around [product], showing the hands, packaging, protective layers, and first reveal in a clean sequence. Make the packaging and product feel accurate and premium, but let the human reaction stay understated and believable. Avoid clutter or excessive props that distract from the reveal.

subjects.title: Making Process
subjects.text: Make the process of creating, preparing, or refining [product] the subject. Show one specific stage with purposeful hands, real tools, material transformation, and visible evidence of care. Keep the craft credible and safe, with accurate tool use and no generic workshop clutter; the product relationship must be clear.

subjects.title: Expert Demonstration
subjects.text: Show a credible expert or knowledgeable user demonstrating [product] in a focused setting. Center the relevant technique, adjustment, or feature, with calm body language and a clear line of sight to the action. The frame should teach one useful thing while keeping product details, hand placement, and results easy to inspect.

subjects.title: Everyday Ritual User
subjects.text: Show [subject] using [product] as part of a quiet daily ritual—beginning the day, pausing, preparing, caring, or winding down. Use a specific, lived-in action and a restrained environment to make the value feel personal. Preserve natural posture, real product use, and small sensory details without making the moment overly styled.

subjects.title: Purposeful Commuter
subjects.text: Show an adult subject moving purposefully through an everyday urban transition—walking, boarding, carrying, or pausing—with [product] integrated naturally into the routine. Use a practical wardrobe, believable personal items, and a clear destination. The product should demonstrate utility without feeling like a conspicuous prop or a staged street-style pose.

subjects.title: Thoughtful Host
subjects.text: Show an adult subject thoughtfully preparing, arranging, or sharing a small experience in which [product] plays a meaningful role. Let the gesture communicate warmth, care, and practical use through real objects and natural interaction. Keep the scene intimate and product-aware rather than overly decorated or performative.

subjects.title: Creative Practitioner
subjects.text: Show an adult creative practitioner using [product] within a focused practice such as sketching, arranging, editing, building, or reviewing. Use a visually coherent workspace with only relevant materials and a relaxed, absorbed expression. Make the product support the practice visibly and credibly, never reduce the person to a generic desk-worker stereotype.

subjects.title: Everyday Outdoor Explorer
subjects.text: Show an adult subject enjoying an accessible outdoor moment—walking a trail, pausing at a viewpoint, cycling nearby, or setting out—with [product] used naturally for the conditions. Use practical, weather-appropriate styling and a specific action. Keep the landscape supportive of the story and preserve the product's realistic fit, scale, and material behavior.

subjects.title: Quiet Reader
subjects.text: Show an adult subject in a quiet, attentive reading or reflection moment with [product] present in a natural, useful role. Use relaxed posture, believable gaze direction, tactile nearby objects, and soft environmental context. The scene should communicate calm focus and personal taste without resorting to clichés or hiding the product.

subjects.title: Friends Sharing a Moment
subjects.text: Show a small, diverse group of adults sharing a spontaneous, respectful everyday moment in which [product] is genuinely useful or enjoyed. Capture natural eye lines, varied expressions, and believable relationships rather than everyone posing toward camera. Keep the product readable and avoid overcrowding the frame with too many people or unrelated activities.

subjects.title: Athletic Recovery Moment
subjects.text: Show an adult subject in a believable post-activity recovery or reset moment with [product] integrated into their routine. Use natural breath, posture, skin texture, and practical athletic styling; the mood should be grounded rather than hyper-performative. Keep the action safe, the product legible, and the environment specific to the activity.

subjects.title: Small-Business Owner
subjects.text: Show an adult small-business owner preparing, checking, packaging, or presenting [product] with quiet confidence. Include only the tools, materials, and work surfaces that make the work credible. The subject should feel like a real operator with a distinctive routine, while the product remains accurate, central, and ready to be understood by customers.

subjects.title: Caregiving Moment
subjects.text: Show [product] supporting a respectful, age-appropriate everyday caregiving or family moment between adults and/or family members. Center practical help, trust, and a natural gesture rather than idealized perfection. Keep roles, products, and interaction clear; avoid sentimentality, clutter, or unsafe product use.

subjects.title: Pet Companion Context
subjects.text: Place [product] in a warm everyday moment that includes a calm companion animal only where it naturally supports the story. Keep the human subject and product as the main focus, with the pet's behavior, scale, fur, and contact physically plausible. Avoid turning the animal into a costume-like accessory or letting it obscure product details.

subjects.title: Confident Direct Portrait
subjects.text: Create a direct, dignified portrait of an adult subject with a relaxed, self-possessed expression and [product] clearly integrated into the frame. Use eye-level connection, natural skin texture, authentic wardrobe, and minimal environmental distractions. Let confidence come from presence and composition, not aggressive posture or excessive retouching.

wardrobeProps.title: Tonal Everyday Basics
wardrobeProps.text: Style the subject in timeless tonal basics—well-fitting tee or knit, simple trousers or denim, clean footwear, and minimal jewelry—in colors that support rather than match or overpower [product]. Prioritize realistic fabric weight, fit, and movement. Keep logos, loud patterns, and trend-specific accessories out of the frame unless they are essential to the story.

wardrobeProps.title: Smart Casual Layering
wardrobeProps.text: Use smart-casual layers with a simple shirt, relaxed tailoring or overshirt, considered trousers, and understated shoes. Choose a restrained palette and believable fit that communicates polish without feeling formal or costume-like. Ensure layers frame the product and permit natural movement; avoid clashing textures, visible unrelated branding, or overly coordinated styling.

wardrobeProps.title: Creative Studio Uniform
wardrobeProps.text: Style a contemporary creative-work uniform: practical overshirt or chore jacket, quality tee or knit, relaxed trousers, and simple durable footwear. Add only one relevant personal detail such as a notebook, pencil, or measuring tape. The outfit should feel worn-in and functional, with colors and textures that support the product or process without turning into a fashion costume.

wardrobeProps.title: Light Outerwear Transition
wardrobeProps.text: Use a lightweight weather layer such as a trench, chore jacket, overshirt, or packable shell over simple base pieces. Make the styling fit a believable transitional-weather situation and allow the outer layer to move naturally. Keep colors quiet, garment construction realistic, and accessories limited so [product] remains visually dominant.

wardrobeProps.title: Minimal Performance Styling
wardrobeProps.text: Use clean, functional activewear in a limited palette: breathable top, practical layer, fitted or relaxed movement pants, and appropriate athletic footwear. Show realistic fabric tension, sweat or weather response only when relevant, and a credible relationship to the activity. Avoid exaggerated futuristic details, loud branding, or accessories that interfere with product visibility.

wardrobeProps.title: Relaxed Home Comfort
wardrobeProps.text: Style a comfortable at-home look with a soft knit, lived-in tee, relaxed trousers, clean socks or simple slippers, and one tactile layer such as a cardigan or overshirt. Keep fabric texture and fit believable, colors calm, and the styling appropriate to the activity. The result should feel personal and real, not like sleepwear advertising or an overly styled interior shoot.

wardrobeProps.title: Purposeful Desk Essentials
wardrobeProps.text: Use a tightly edited desk set: one notebook or sketchbook, a quality pen or pencil, a cup or glass, one relevant device or tool, and a restrained surface texture. Arrange items to support the subject's task and lead the eye toward [product]. Keep screens generic or blank, remove visual clutter, and avoid using props solely as decoration.

wardrobeProps.title: Material Sample Library
wardrobeProps.text: Surround [product] with a small, curated selection of related material samples—swatches, grains, fibers, ingredients, components, or finish chips—to make quality and construction tangible. Keep every sample relevant in scale and color, with clear separation from the hero product. Use them as evidence of craft, not as decorative confetti.

wardrobeProps.title: Familiar Scale Object
wardrobeProps.text: Use one familiar, contextually relevant object to establish the scale of [product], such as a hand, book, cup, key, standard work tool, or everyday surface. Keep the comparison honest and visually secondary. Do not use an object that misleads about size, competes with the product, or introduces unrelated brand marks.

wardrobeProps.title: Practical Travel Edit
wardrobeProps.text: Use a concise travel styling edit: comfortable layer, practical shoes, small bag or carry-on, water bottle, paper ticket or neutral map, and one weather-appropriate accessory. Every piece should support a credible journey and reveal how [product] travels or fits into a routine. Avoid excessive airport clichés, fake labels, or decorative luggage clutter.

wardrobeProps.title: Tabletop Ritual Props
wardrobeProps.text: Build a small tabletop ritual around [product] with two to four useful companion objects: ceramic vessel, folded linen, ingredient, book, tray, or tool appropriate to the story. Use tactile materials and restrained color so the set feels intentional and usable. Leave breathing room, preserve the hero product's silhouette, and avoid overfilling the frame.

wardrobeProps.title: Fresh Ingredient Accent
wardrobeProps.text: Use a small, fresh selection of real ingredients, botanicals, or natural elements only when they truthfully support the product's use, origin, or sensory story. Keep them hydrated, physically plausible, and arranged with restrained asymmetry. Their color and texture may add contrast, but they must never obscure [product] or imply unsupported ingredients or claims.

wardrobeProps.title: Reading & Reflection Accessories
wardrobeProps.text: Use a quiet set of reading and reflection accessories—an open book or magazine with non-readable generic pages, a pen, a textured throw, and a warm drink—to support a calm human moment. Keep the objects partially used rather than perfectly staged. Ensure [product] has a meaningful role and remains the focal point.

wardrobeProps.title: Restrained Floral Gesture
wardrobeProps.text: Use one restrained botanical or floral gesture, such as a single stem, small branch, or simple vessel arrangement, to introduce natural shape and color. Match its scale and palette to [product] and the setting. Keep it secondary, believable for the location, and free from excessive blooms, petals, or artificial-looking decoration.

wardrobeProps.title: Mirror & Reflection Accent
wardrobeProps.text: Use a small mirror, reflective tile, or polished surface to reveal a complementary angle of [product] or add controlled depth to the frame. Match the reflection's perspective, lighting, and scale precisely. Keep reflected content clean and purposeful; avoid visual duplicates, distorted logos, glare that hides features, or reflections that confuse the product form.

wardrobeProps.title: Simple Pedestal Riser
wardrobeProps.text: Present [product] on a simple cylinder, block, plinth, or folded surface that adds elevation and depth without competing for attention. Match the riser’s material, color, and scale to the product story; use soft shadows to ground it. Avoid precarious placement, excessive stacked forms, or a pedestal so ornate that it becomes the subject.

wardrobeProps.title: Packaging Context
wardrobeProps.text: Include the product's accurate packaging only when it improves understanding of the purchase, delivery, gift, or unboxing story. Preserve exact branding, color, structure, and scale; position packaging so it supports rather than hides the hero product. Use minimal tissue, ribbon, insert, or label details, with no invented copy, logos, or excess wrapping.

wardrobeProps.title: Practical Carry Accessories
wardrobeProps.text: Use a few real-world carry accessories that make [product]'s role tangible: a neutral tote, compact pouch, keys, water bottle, headphones, or notebook. Keep the selection limited and activity-specific, with believable wear and scale. Avoid a cluttered flat lay, visible competing brand marks, or accessories that obscure the product.

wardrobeProps.title: Relevant Craft Tools
wardrobeProps.text: Use only the tools genuinely associated with making, maintaining, or using [product], such as a brush, measuring tool, scissors, palette knife, or assembly implement. Show correct scale, safe handling, and a partially completed action. Keep the tool set edited and functional; avoid generic tool clutter or inaccurate craft symbolism.

wardrobeProps.title: Seasonal Texture Layer
wardrobeProps.text: Introduce one seasonally appropriate texture—light cotton, woven linen, wool knit, rain shell, or softly weathered layer—to communicate conditions without relying on literal seasonal décor. Make fabric weight, folds, and thermal logic believable for the setting. Use the layer to frame [product] or human action, never to cover key details.
